small_guidance:
- Add larger N-tiles to the autotune list (e.g. (64,128,32), (128,128,32), (64,256,32)) at num_warps=8, num_stages=2 — OUT_SP=30·62·62≈115k is huge so wider BLOCK_N amortizes the weight load across more output positions; verify (BM·BK+BK·BN)·4·ns ≤ 132KB.
- K_TOTAL=216 is small (8·27); try BLOCK_K=32 or 64 so the K-loop has only 4-7 iterations and the inner tl.dot is well-shaped, and drop BLOCK_K=16 configs that just add loop overhead.
- Drop the GROUP_SP swizzle (it's a no-op as written: group_id*GROUP_SP+in_group == pid_sp_raw) and instead swizzle pid_n_oc so the same OC tile is reused across adjacent spatial tiles, improving L2 hit rate on the weight tile.
large_guidance:
- Switch input layout to NDHWC (channels-last) so the GEMM-K dimension (ic, kd, kh, kw) is contiguous in memory; in the current NCDHW layout, ic-stride=ID·IH·IW makes BLOCK_K loads strided and uncoalesced, which is likely the dominant bottleneck given fast_p≈1.95 vs theoretical headroom.
- Persistent-CTA design: launch one program per SM, loop over (n, oc_tile, sp_tile) tiles internally so weight tiles can be reused across multiple spatial tiles within the same program without re-loading from HBM; OC=32 is tiny (one BLOCK_M=32 tile covers it) so the whole weight matrix (32×216 = ~27KB) fits in SMEM/registers once.
- Since OC·K_TOTAL = 32·216 ≈ 6912 fp32 fits easily in SMEM, preload the entire weight matrix once per program and stream only x through the K loop — converts the kernel from a generic GEMM into a specialized small-OC convolution.
